newsitem.title: CHINA: Citibank opens branch in Shanghai's Pudong.
newsitem.headline: Citibank opens branch in Shanghai's Pudong.

text.p: Citibank NA expects the Chinese local currency business to be profitable almost from day one but volumes to be relatively modest, at least for the rest of this year, a senior bank executive said on Monday.

John Beeman, Citibank's country corporate officer for China, told a news conference the bank expected the Chinese central bank to issue detailed regulations covering foreign banks doing Chinese yuan business in March.

"There will then be a thorough inspection of our branch premises and procedures. Assuming we pass the inspection, we hope to be able to offer (local currency) products and services in April," he said.
Citibank on Monday formally opened a full branch office in Shanghai's Pudong development zone, meeting a key requirement to obtain the right to handle local currency business.
It is one of eight foreign banks that have so far been given approval to do Chinese yuan business. Up to now, all foreign banks in China have been restricted to doing foreign currency transactions.
"On the scale (of the local currency business), our expectation at least for this year is that it will probably be relatively modest," Beeman said.
"On profitability, it depends how you do the accounting. But I would expect it to be profitable in terms of operating income almost from the beginning," he added.
He said Citibank's current branch office in the central Puxi area of Shanghai was being converted into a sub-branch and would not be able to offer local currency services for the time being.
But he said he saw the Chinese authorities relaxing restrictions and expanding the scope for foreign banks to do local currency business once they were satisfied with the way things were working.
"We believe the intention is to let all foreign bank branches (around the country) eventually do local currency business, hopefully not too far in the future," he said.

Preliminary regulations already issued by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, require the volume of Chinese yuan business be no more than 35 percent of the volume of a bank's foreign exchange business.
They are also restricted to taking deposits and making loans to foreign-invested enterprises, and Chinese firms that have obtained special approval.
In the initial stages, the banks are also required to only do business with foreign-invested firms registered in Shanghai.

Beeman said Citibank was looking forward to doing local currency business, adding: "Citibank does business in around 100 countries, and in only two of them are we unable to do local currency business -- China and one African country."
